newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate eases 20 bps to 11.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate eases 20 bps to 11.1 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate edged down 20 basis points to 11.1 percent on Monday because of an inflow of fresh kuna funds.
Daily settlements totalled 39.9 million kuna, against 120 million on offer. New deals accounted for 21.7 million kuna, mostly call money loans granted at an unchanged 8.0 percent.
Term loans were struck at 10 percent for one-week and 15 percent for one-month loans, while two-month borrowings were made at 18 percent, up from 17 percent.
Banks extended previous loans at rates varying from 10.5 percent for one-week deals to 16 percent for one-year deals.
Savings banks rolled over previous two-week loans at 13 percent.
The central bank's kuna midrates for Tuesday eased to 6.3794 to the dollar and firmed to 3.5639 to the German mark.
